request.prompt: Create a strong HAVENLINE World 1 purchase-value upgrade concept sheet, using the supplied references as the retained base identity and scale anchors. Chunky rounded stylized 3D mobile-game art: warm orange timber, deep blue painted metal, rounded gray hardware and softly sculpted snow. Clean navy studio ground, controlled lighting and clear silhouettes. The upgrades must visibly add working structure and a useful operation, not just thicker brackets or a recolor. Make EXACTLY two rows by three roomy columns, six substantial panels. Top row is the first new proposal; bottom row is the later new proposal. Within each row show the SAME physical design in exterior front three-quarter, genuine opposite rear three-quarter, and an open/cutaway functional view. Keep a consistent scale and physical coordinate system within each row. The functional view is the same object with roof/guard hidden, never an extra design. Preserve approved ordinary resource size and standard conveyor width/height. Bigger buildings and new ports are authored upgrades with clear purchased ground area, not enlarged resources or a new belt skin. Do not show the old base as a newly designed third stage. Titles and short stage/view labels only; no numerical levels, prices, yields, capacity or rate claims. Footer: AUTHORED UPGRADE PROPOSAL. No workers, UI, magic energy, electric fields or unsupported fuel system. This is proposed design, not proof of runtime implementation. HEADER: HAVENLINE / SAWMILL PROGRESSION. TOP ROW label FEED MILL. Build one visibly elongated log-feed mill: left raw-log cradle with a real metering gate -> captive clamped feed bed -> one guarded circular cutting head -> right plank stack cradle. Include one front-side manual crank physically linked to the cutter and feed rollers and clear continuous front service lane. Its long mechanical feed bed and output stacker must be large readable additions to the original small saw table. BOTTOM ROW label PARALLEL SAWMILL. Build a substantially wider twin-bay lumber works with TWO parallel feed beds, TWO guarded circular saw heads, TWO independent plank outfeed cradles, a shared raised receiving rack and one small mechanical stacking arm. Give each cutting lane its own reachable front manual crank and independently staffed workstation; there is no automatic or unexplained power. Give it a partial timber canopy and blue structural frames, keeping both complete material paths visible. Both lanes enter from the same left receiving side and discharge to the same right dispatch side in every view; front is always the unobstructed worker-control aisle. Show clear ground aprons and an explicit empty gap between the parallel work cells. Place only a few correctly scaled raw wood logs at infeed and existing plank stacks at outfeed. Guards and frame cannot block these paths. Third panel of each row is a cutaway from above and the front, revealing the actual clamp/blade/output relationship, with exactly the same machine as the other two views. Short view captions FRONT / REAR / FUNCTION. Do not depict a generic steam factory, floating planks, decorative gears without a path, extra recipes or a claim of more planks from the same wood. Full output holds only its affected lane; the picture should show separate output cradles rather than a shared blocked bottleneck.
